what_its_for: Cidofovir is an antiviral medicine used to treat a serious eye infection called CMV retinitis (cytomegalovirus retinitis) in people with AIDS. This infection can cause vision loss or blindness if not treated. Cidofovir works by slowing down the growth of the CMV virus to help protect your eyesight.
how_to_take: Cidofovir is given as an IV (intravenous) infusion directly into your vein by a healthcare provider in a clinic or hospital setting. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home. Each infusion usually takes about 1 hour. Before each cidofovir infusion, you MUST take a medicine called probenecid by mouth AND receive IV fluids (saline) to protect your kidneys. Always follow your doctor's and nurse's instructions exactly on the day of your infusion.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your weight and kidney function. The typical schedule is: one infusion once a week for 2 weeks (called the 'induction' phase), then one infusion every 2 weeks after that (called the 'maintenance' phase). You will also take probenecid pills (usually 2 grams) 3 hours before your infusion and again (1 gram each time) at 2 hours and 8 hours after your infusion. Do not miss your probenecid doses — they are very important to protect your kidneys.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare provider, contact your doctor or clinic right away if you need to reschedule or miss an appointment. Do not try to make up a missed dose on your own. Keeping all scheduled appointments is very important to keep the virus under control and protect your vision.
storage: Cidofovir is stored and handled by your healthcare provider or pharmacy. If you are given probenecid tablets to take at home, store them at room temperature (59°F to 77°F / 15°C to 25°C), away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking NSAIDs (like ibuprofen, naproxen, aspirin) or other medicines that can harm your kidneys around the time of your infusion, unless your doctor says it is safe. Avoid other kidney-damaging medicines such as aminoglycoside antibiotics, amphotericin B, or IV pentamidine within 7 days of your cidofovir dose. Do not breastfeed while using this medicine. Use reliable birth control during treatment — cidofovir can cause serious birth defects. Men should use condoms during and for 3 months after treatment because cidofovir may be found in semen. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: decreased urination or no urination (a sign of kidney problems), swelling in your legs or ankles, unusual weight gain, vision changes or worsening eye symptoms, severe nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain after taking probenecid, signs of low white blood cells such as fever, chills, or signs of infection, eye pain or increased floaters, or any allergic reaction such as rash, hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face or throat.
when_it_works: Cidofovir does not cure CMV retinitis, but it helps slow down the virus and prevent your vision from getting worse. You may not feel or see a difference right away. It is important to keep all your infusion appointments even if you feel well, because stopping treatment can allow the virus to become active again. Your eye doctor will check your eyes regularly to see how well the medicine is working.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Cidofovir can cause serious kidney damage. Your kidney function will be checked with blood and urine tests before every dose. The dose may be reduced or stopped if your kidneys are not working well. This medicine should NOT be used if you already have moderate to severe kidney disease. Pregnancy: Cidofovir can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Tell your doctor immediately if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Women of childbearing age must use effective birth control during treatment and for 1 month after the last dose. Men should use barrier contraception (condoms) during treatment and for 3 months after stopping. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to kidney side effects. Close monitoring is needed. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been fully established. Use in children should only be under close medical supervision.
